items.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997
items.q: Jimmy Rowles is where I should have stayed.

ctx.x: She gets a very nice sound on the piano and very good time. She’s one of the best. But she’s singing now so I don’t know what that’s about. But maybe that’s how they’re pushing her. But I think that’s a contemporary player. She has a couple of good guys

working with her. But they don’t have any drums, they just have a bass — Nat Cole voicings you know, uh, instrumentation, not voicing. And she was going to study, she was studying with Jimmy Rowles . And I played with them one night. Her mother and father said, “Will you play with them, play behind my daughter some night?” I said, “Sure, okay.” So we played Donte’s and she was very thankful. I says, “What are you going to do now?” She says, “Oh I’m going to Canada and study with Don Thompson.” I said, “Aren’t you…
Well I’ll tell you this has been a fascinating hour to speak to you.
